transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I hope I'm doing this right, but I guess I came in because I've been feeling a little overwhelmed lately. I'm a financial advisor here in Cincinnati, and... well, I know this might sound a little strange, so please bear with me. 

For a while now, I’ve been kind of convinced that certain people in the arts and finance circles around town are... quietly tracking which clients I meet with. And, um, it feels like they're sending me these little signals about it. Like through the networking invitations I get, or the topics at panels, or even just who happens to sit near me at events. 

I keep telling myself it could just be a coincidence, you know? I really try to be rational about it. But... I just can’t really seem to let it go. Is that... does that make sense to bring up here? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Do you think it's possible that these people are not actually tracking you or sending you signals?

Oh, definitely. I mean, yes, I completely agree with you that it's possible. I actually try to tell myself that all the time. I really don't want you to think I'm... you know, totally unreasonable or anything. I know exactly how it sounds. 

But... even when I sit down and logically tell myself that it could just be a coincidence—that maybe the networking invitations, or the specific panel topics, or even just who happens to sit next to me at these events aren't actually signals about which clients I'm meeting with... I just... I still can't really seem to let it go. It just feels so deliberate when it happens, no matter how hard I try to brush it off. 

Am I making sense? I'm really trying my best to look at it rationally, I promise.
How long have you been having these thoughts about being tracked and receiving signals?

Um... let me think. I guess it hasn't been too long, really. Just... maybe about two months? I've been trying my best to just work through it on my own, so I hope it's okay that I waited a little bit to come in and talk to someone. 

But yeah, I'd say it's been right around two months since I started feeling like people were tracking my client meetings and sending those signals. Is... is that helpful? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline.
Have you been acting on these beliefs about being tracked, or have they been more of a worry for you?

Well... mostly it’s just been a worry, really. I want to assure you I’m definitely still working, and I try my absolute hardest not to let it affect my job. I really pride myself on being a good advisor. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest—and I hope you don't think less of me for this—my practice has gotten a little bit smaller recently. I’ve just... well, I've missed a few follow-ups here and there, and I kind of started avoiding some of the public panels, just to keep my head down. It’s just been a little harder to keep up the exact same level of client contact that I used to manage so easily. 

But I am still working, I promise! I'm really trying to push through it and do a good job. Did I... did I answer that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you think these people are actually capable of tracking your client meetings and sending you signals, or is it just a feeling you have?

Well... I mean, when you put it like that, it sounds a little out there, I know. And I really, really try to tell myself it's just a feeling. But... I guess I do kind of believe they're actually capable of it. 

The arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati are pretty tight-knit, you know? It wouldn't be impossible for people to talk or to know who I'm meeting with. So when I see those little signals—like the specific invitations, or the panel topics that just happen to align perfectly with what I'm working on, or even just who ends up sitting near me at these events—it just... it feels so real. 

I know I said earlier that I try to brush it off as a coincidence, and I really do try, I promise. But deep down, I guess I am kind of convinced that they are actually doing it. I just can't seem to shake it. Does that make sense? I hope that doesn't make me sound too... you know, irrational. I'm really trying to be objective about it.
Have these thoughts about being tracked and receiving signals affected your relationships with friends or family?

Um... I really try not to let it burden anyone, I promise. My friends and family are wonderful, and I'd never want to push them away. But... I guess if I look at it honestly, it has affected things a little bit. 

I just... I don't seem to have the same spark lately, if that makes sense? Like I mentioned, I still get my work done, just in pieces, but I'll leave those client follow-ups sitting longer than I normally ever would. And with my friends... well, I've been skipping our usual jazz nights and the pickup basketball games we usually play. And the part I feel really guilty about is that I don't even feel much about missing them. I know that sounds terrible, and I really hope you don't think I'm a bad friend for saying that. 

It's just... when they ask me what's going on or check in on me, I end up giving really short answers. Not because I don't care about them! I really do. It's just because... well, talking just feels like so much more effort than it should right now. It just takes it out of me. 

Is... is that a normal way to react to all this? I just want to make sure I'm not doing something completely wrong by pulling back a little.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your daily routine or activities since these thoughts about being tracked started?

Um... I wouldn't say there have been *significant* changes, no. I'm really trying to keep everything as normal as possible. I mean, I still get up, I still go to work, I still do what I need to do. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around the house all day or anything like that.

I guess... well, like I said, I haven't been going to jazz nights or playing basketball as much. And maybe I spend a little more time at home just... resting, I suppose. Just trying to recharge because everything feels a bit exhausting lately. But my basic day-to-day routine is mostly the same, I promise. I'm really doing my best to stay on top of things. 

Did I... does that answer what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do you think these beliefs about being tracked are definitely true, or are you still unsure about them?

Well... I mean, I really, really try to tell myself it's just a coincidence, you know? Like I said before, I try to be rational about it. I don't want to be someone who just believes crazy things. But... if I'm being completely honest, and I know this might sound bad... I guess I am pretty convinced that it's actually happening. 

It's just that it's been going on for a while now, this feeling that these people in the arts and finance circles are quietly tracking my client meetings. And the little signals—the invitations, the panel topics, the seating arrangements at events—they just feel too specific to ignore, even when I try my hardest to brush them off. I just can't really let it go, no matter how much I tell myself I should. 

I know that probably sounds a bit unreasonable, and I'm really sorry if it makes me seem... well, a bit unhinged. I promise I'm trying to look at it objectively. Do you think it's okay that I still feel this way, even though I'm trying not to?
Do you believe that the signals you're receiving are specifically intended for you, or could they be meant for someone else?

Um... well, I really hope this doesn't make me sound self-centered or anything. I try to stay humble, I really do. But... yes, I do think they're meant specifically for me. 

It's just that the things I notice—the invitations to certain events, the specific topics they choose for the panels, and even who they seat near me... it all just aligns too perfectly with the clients I've been meeting with here in Cincinnati. If it was just one or two things, maybe it could be for someone else, but it all just feels so tailored to my schedule and my work in the finance and arts circles. 

I know it sounds a little presumptuous to think people are going through all that trouble just for me. I really try to tell myself I'm not that important, and maybe it is just a coincidence like I said before. But the signals just keep happening, and I just can't shake the feeling that they're directed at me. 

Is it... is it terribly arrogant of me to think that way? I don't want to come across as someone who thinks the world revolves around them. I'm just trying to be honest about what I'm experiencing.
Have you felt like these thoughts about being tracked have significantly impacted your overall well-being or daily life?

Um... I wouldn't say *significantly* impacted, no. I mean, I'm still working, and I'm really trying to keep everything running smoothly. I definitely don't want you to think my life is falling apart or anything like that. I'm still seeing clients and doing my job. 

I guess... well, if I'm being completely honest, and I know this might not sound great... my practice has gotten a little bit smaller lately. I've just been... maybe missing a few follow-ups here and there. And I have been avoiding some of the public panels, just because of how overwhelming the signals feel. It's just gotten a little harder to keep up the exact same level of client contact I used to manage. 

But I'm really trying my best to stay on top of it, I promise. I don't want to seem like I'm slacking off or letting my career go. It's just... it takes a lot of energy to deal with all this, you know? Does that make sense? I hope that doesn't make me sound incompetent. I'm really trying to handle it all as well as I can.
Do you believe that the signals or messages you're receiving are somehow related to your own thoughts or actions?

Um... I don't really think so. I mean, I try to be very careful about what I do and say, so I don't think I'm doing anything to cause this. 

Like I said, it's mostly about the seating arrangements and the invitations and things like that. I don't feel like they're responding to my thoughts or anything... magical like that. I know that would sound really crazy, and I promise I don't believe anything like that. It's just the external things, the events and the people I interact with. 

I hope that's the right way to look at it? I'm really trying to keep a level head about all of this and not let my imagination run away with me. I definitely don't think they can read my mind or anything, if that's what you mean. Does that sound reasonable to you?
Do you believe that the signals or events you've mentioned are specifically about you or your actions, rather than just coincidences?

Um... well, yes. I know I touched on some of this already, and I really, really try to tell myself that it’s all just a coincidence. I want to be completely rational about it, I promise. I don't want to come across as... well, paranoid or anything like that. 

But... I just can't really let it go. If I'm being completely honest—and I hope this doesn't make you think less of me—for a while now I’ve been pretty convinced that certain people in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati are quietly tracking exactly which clients I meet with. So, yes, it is about my actions, specifically my work with my clients. 

And then they send me those little signals, like I mentioned, through the invitations, the panel topics, and even who sits near me at the networking events. I constantly tell myself it could just be a coincidence, because I know exactly how all this must sound to you. I really try to brush it off. But it just happens so consistently with my client list that I can't seem to shake it. 

I hope you understand why I'm struggling with it so much. I'm not making a fool of myself by admitting all this, am I? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you think the signals you're receiving are meant to convey a specific message about you or your actions?

Um... no, I wouldn't say there's a specific message. I want to make sure I'm answering this right, but... it's not like they're trying to tell me to do something, or giving me instructions or anything. I know that would probably be really concerning, and I promise I'm not experiencing anything like that. 

It feels more just like... a nudge, I guess? Just them letting me know they see who I'm working with. But there's no actual message or hidden meaning that I'm supposed to decode. I try really hard not to overthink it, because I don't want to go down a rabbit hole and start sounding completely unreasonable to you. 

So, no, no specific messages about me or what I should do. I really hope that's a good thing? I want to stay as grounded as possible through all this, and I'm really trying not to read too much into it. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for.
Do you feel like these thoughts about being tracked have made it harder for you to enjoy your daily activities or maintain your usual level of productivity?

Um... well, I wouldn't say it's ruined my life or anything. I'm still working, and I still have my clients. I really want to emphasize that I haven't just given up or stopped trying. I'm still a functioning professional.

But... I guess if I'm being completely honest, and I know I need to be honest with you... things have slowed down a little bit. My practice has gotten a bit smaller. It's just that sometimes I... well, I might miss a follow-up call here and there, or I might decide not to attend certain public panels if I feel like the seating or the topics are going to be... you know, focused on me. 

It's just gotten a little harder to keep up the exact same level of client contact I used to manage. I'm still doing my job, I promise, it's just... maybe not at 110% right now. I really hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or incapable. I'm trying my best to push through it and not let it affect my work too much. Is it normal for things to slip just a little bit when you're dealing with stress like this? I just want to make sure I'm handling this the right way.
Have you noticed a significant decline in your ability to function at work or in social situations since these thoughts started?

Um... well, like I was just saying, I wouldn't call it a *significant* decline. I'm really trying to make sure I don't give you the wrong impression here. I'm definitely still working, still seeing clients, still functioning. I haven't fallen apart or anything like that, I promise.

It's just... maybe a little bit of a dip? Like I mentioned, my practice has gotten a little smaller. I guess I have missed a few follow-ups, and I do avoid some of those public panels now, just to be safe. And it is a bit harder to keep up that really high level of client contact I used to have. But I'm still doing my job, you know? I'm still a professional. 

I really hope that doesn't sound like a massive failure on my part. I'm trying so hard to keep everything on track. Do you think it's understandable that I've scaled back just a tiny bit, given everything? I just want to make sure I'm not sounding like I've completely lost control of my work.
Do you think the signals you're receiving are meant for you alone, or could someone else also be receiving similar signals?

Um... that's a good question. I... I honestly don't think anyone else is getting them. It feels pretty specific to me. 

But I want to be clear, I don't think that makes me special or important or anything like that! I know sometimes people who experience things like this can get... well, a bit grandiose, right? And I promise I don't feel that way at all. I'm just a regular financial advisor, trying to do my job. 

It's just that the nudges, the little signs... they seem tied to the specific clients I'm working with, so it wouldn't really make sense for someone else to be getting them. But I definitely don't think it's some grand conspiracy focused on me. I'm trying to be really rational about the whole thing. Does that sound like a reasonable way to look at it? I hope I'm making sense and not sounding too... self-centered or anything.
Have you ever had a period of time where you didn't believe you were being tracked or receiving these signals?

Oh, definitely. I mean, for almost my entire life I never thought anything like this was happening. I really want to make sure you know this isn't, like, my normal state of being. I've always been very grounded and focused on my career. 

It's actually a pretty recent thing. I'd say... um, maybe it's only been going on for about two months? Yeah, just the last two months or so is when I started noticing the signals and getting the feeling that people were tracking my client meetings. Before that, everything was completely standard. 

I really hope that's a good sign, right? The fact that it's only been a couple of months? I'm hoping it just means it's a temporary phase and I'll be back to my old self soon. Does that sound like a positive thing to you, that it hasn't been happening for very long?
Have you ever had a time, even briefly, where you completely stopped believing you were being tracked?

Um... I really wish I could say yes, because I want to be completely rational about all this. And I do try! I really try to talk myself out of it. I'll sit down and tell myself that maybe it's just a coincidence that these people in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati are doing all this. Like, maybe the invitations I get, or the specific panel topics, or even who happens to sit right near me at events... maybe they aren't actually little signals, you know? I try to convince myself they aren't quietly tracking which clients I meet with. 

But... even when I tell myself it could just be a coincidence, I... I can't really let it go. The feeling just kind of stays there, no matter how hard I try to shake it. I hope that doesn't make me sound too stubborn or, um, unreasonable. I'm really trying my best to think critically about it, I promise. Do you think it makes sense that it's hard to just turn off a feeling like that once you've noticed the pattern?
Have you ever had a moment, no matter how brief, where you did not believe you were being tracked?

I know I just mentioned this, and I really don't want to sound like a broken record, but... no. Not completely. 

I mean, I really try to step back and look at it objectively. I'll tell myself, "Okay, you're a financial advisor in Cincinnati, you go to these arts and finance events, of course you're going to see the same people, of course the topics might overlap with your work." I try to tell myself that the invitations and who sits next to me are just normal networking things, not them quietly tracking my client meetings or sending me little signals. 

But even when I lay it all out like that, logically... the feeling that it's all connected just won't go away. I can't seem to just brush it off as a coincidence, even when I really, really want to. I know that probably sounds a bit irrational, right? I'm sorry if I'm not giving you the answer you're looking for. I just want to be as honest with you as I can. Is it normal to struggle this much to talk yourself out of something?
Have you ever had a period where you didn't think about being tracked for a whole day?

A whole day? Um... gosh, I really wish I could say yes. I'd love to tell you I can just turn it off completely for a day. I try so hard to just focus on my work and be productive, because I want to be a good professional. 

But... if I'm being completely honest—and I know I keep coming back to the same thing, I'm so sorry—it's... it's a no. Not a full day. Even if I manage to distract myself for a few hours in the morning, eventually I'll check my email and see an invitation, or hear about a new panel topic going around the arts and finance circles, or I'll remember who sat near me at the last event. And... the feeling just creeps right back in. That they're quietly tracking my client meetings and sending me those little signals. 

I always tell myself it's just a coincidence, just like we talked about, but I just can't seem to let it go for a full twenty-four hours. I'm really sorry if that's not the answer you're hoping to hear. I promise I'm trying my absolute best to ignore it and push through. Am I doing okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to help me.
